passage: At 1 a. m. of the 3d, Muhlenberg's (F, Fourth United States, six 12-poun(iers) and Kinzie's (K, Fifth United States, four 12-pounders) batteries were posted opposite the center of the line of the Twelfth Corps, so as to command the ravine formed by Rock Creek.
note: Time (01:00 Jul 3), batteries, and place (opposite the center of the XII Corps line, commanding the Rock Creek ravine) all stated; Muhlenberg p870 adds 'parallel to and on the southwest side of the Baltimore pike, almost directly opposite the center of the line formed by the Twelfth'.

passage: After dark, I -withdre-w, and leaving a picket on the Hanover road, joined the rest of the division in rear of the enemy's breastworks
note: No Lt. Edgar and no 75-man detail in the cited pages. OR shows a different picket episode: Walker leaves a picket on the Hanover road after dark; Nadenbousch p522: companies 'detached on the evening of the 2d instant, and left in rear on picket to guard the Hanover road'. Row's 'go forward as pickets a few hours after midnight; brigade rejoined after dark' differs in direction and hour. Only source SWB3 (secondary).
No OR citation; row is an open gap (Confederate Jul 3 night camps, fires, burying parties; Pickett presence disputed). Nothing to verify.
No OR citation; row is an explicit design hypothesis (rear fires, none on contact lines), unsourced. Nothing to verify.

passage: During the night the line was strengthened as much as possible with rails, stones, and earth thrown up with sticks and boards, no tools being obtainable.
note: Hall p437 (page ~437): line strengthened in the night with rails, stones and earth; Curtis p450: 'Though but one spade could be obtained, the rails were nearly covered with earth by daylight'; Harrow p420: 'The entire line was strengthened during the night by such means as could be commanded'; Tyler p873: 'all the reserve batteries (twelve in number) ... in position' and 'The infantry had constructed a slight breastwork of such materials as the ground afforded along the entire crest'. NOT supported: that the work was on 'the stone wall' (not stated; Hall's brigade was left of the Copse) or that the Angle wall was a pre-existing 2-3 ft farm wall; 'before dawn' is by inference ('by daylight'); Hunt personally bringing up reserve batteries is not on these pages. OR evidences rail/earth reinforcement, contrary to the row's 'unverified'; do not apply it to the pre-existing Angle wall.

passage: At 4.30 a. m. these batteries opened, and fired without intermission for fifteen minutes into the wood, at a range of from 600 to 800 yards.
note: Event (Union artillery fire on the Confederates in the Culp's Hill works at dawn, followed by Johnson's attack; Ewell p447: 'Half an hour after Johnson attacked, and when too late to recall him') supported, but the OR hours conflict: Candy p836 'until 3.45 a. m. [July 3], when the enemy were opened upon by a battery'; Geary p828 '(early dawn) a simultaneous attack ... by artillery and the infantry'; Kane p847 'attack in force upon us commenced at 3.30 a. m.' (Confederate attack); Hunt p237 04:30 for Muhlenberg/Kinzie (15 min) and 5.30 for all batteries; Greene p857 artillery opened, 'attack was general ... until 10.30 a.' NOT supported: 'five batteries, 24 guns', '30 minutes to several hours', 03:30-04:30 as one window. Ewell's 'too late to recall' refers to notice about Longstreet, not an order from Lee.

passage: as the re-enforcements had to be in position before daylight, I was compelled to- send to General Johnson the troops of my second line, i. e., the brigades of Daniel and O'Neal (excepting the Fifth Alabama).
note: Rodes: Daniel's and O'Neal's brigades sent to Johnson to be in position before daylight; Johnson p504: 'Daniel's and Rodes' brigades (Colonel O'Neal commanding) ... having reported to me'; Lee p320: Ewell 'during the night, re-enforced General Johnson with two brigades from Rodes' and one from Early's division'. NOT supported: ~04:00 hour (OR says 'before daylight'), forming 'behind Nicholls and Jones', 'four brigades' (OR: three or two).

passage: the breastworks on the left of swale, being the whole original position of the First and of part of the Third Brigade, were found to be occupied by the enemy in force.
note: Event (XII Corps returns and finds Confederates in its works) supported by Ruger p780 and Colgrove p813 ('They shortly returned with 23 prisoners, and reported that the enemy held our works on the left in large force', 'owing to the darkness of the night'), Geary p827 (Kane fired on from the works). The OR places the discovery on the night of Jul 2, not ~04:00 Jul 3; Ruger notes fire opened 'on the morning of July 3'. Row's ~04:00 hour is not supported (and conflicts with T2-230). 'Spangler's Spring' not named.

passage: About midnight. I received orders from Colonel Alexander, commanding reserve artillery, to take position on the field before dayliglit, and with his assistance I placed my battalion, consistmg of eight Napoleon guns and two 13-pounder howitzers,
note: Eshleman p434: orders about midnight to take position before daylight; Miller's guns 'about 100 yards to the left of the peach orchard'; Norcom and Richardson on the left; 'Major Dearing afterward took position with his battalion on my left, and five guns of Colonel Cabell's battalion were placed in position between Captains Norcom and Richardson' (note: Dearing took position 'afterward' and the left was moved at daybreak, so before-daylight placement applies to Eshleman's own battalion).
Computed civil twilight/sunrise/solar position (ephemeris_1863.json); no OR claim. Not OR-checkable.

passage: these batteries opened, and fired without intermission for fifteen minutes into the wood, at a range of from 600 to 800 yards.
note: Hunt p237: Muhlenberg's and Kinzie's batteries ('At 4.30 a. m. these batteries opened'), fifteen minutes, 600-800 yards; Muhlenberg p870: 'two rifle batteries (ten guns) and the two light 12-pounder batteries (ten guns) opened, and fired for fifteen minutes without intermission at a range of from 600 to 800 yards'. Hour 04:30 per Hunt (the OR hours for the Culp's Hill opening conflict, see T2-242; Muhlenberg's own hour not re-read).

passage: E.] Richardson's company (A) was thrown out early in the day as sharpshooters, and were not m the mam engagement, but did good service as sharpshooters,
note: Maffett (3rd SC Bn, Kershaw): only Company A thrown out as sharpshooters on Jul 2 (Rose/Wheatfield sector); no rounds-per-man figure, no 'over 200 rounds by morning of Jul 3'; Berdan's 95 rounds at Pitzer's Woods also not in OR. Row rests on American Rifleman (secondary); keep as visible gap, do not attach to a unit.

passage: He arrived in the afternoon of the following day, and took position on General Ewell's left.
note: Lee (Jan 1864 report p322): Stuart arrived 'in the afternoon of the following day' (Jul 2) and took position on Ewell's left; Hampton's leading brigade repulsed enemy cavalry at Hunterstown; Stuart p697: 'My advance reached Gettysburg July 2'; 'I took my position that day on the York and Heidlersburg roads'. NOT supported: arrival hour (OR only 'afternoon'), brigades arriving 'that evening', Lee's reproach, Stuart meeting Lee at HQ on Seminary Ridge.

passage: he attempted a charge, which was met in front by the Cobb Legion, while I threw the Phillips Legion and the Second South Carolina as supporting forces on each flank of the enemy.
note: Hunterstown Jul 2 supported: Hampton p724 (Cobb, Phillips Legion, 2nd SC; 'Night coming on, I held the ground until morning'); Green p497 (Louisiana Guard Artillery): 'Arrived at dusk, and immediately engaged a battery attached to the enemy's cavalry ... The engagement lasted until dark ... Fell back a mile, and took up another position, in which we remained until morning'; Kilpatrick p992 'attacked ... at sundown near Hunterstown'. NOT supported: Custer's Co. A, 6th Michigan charge, Custer's horse/Churchill, 'Hampton withdraws toward Gettysburg and camps north of town' (OR: held ground / fell back a mile). Hampton's wound is Jul 3 in the OR (Lee p298/322, Green p498), not at Hunterstown. Conflict carried.

passage: The First and Third Brigades, of the Second Division, Cavalry Corps, arrived on the battle-field at Gettysburg, July 2, about noon, the Second Brigade having been sent to Westminster.
note: Gregg p956: arrival about noon; placed on the extreme right at the Hanover turnpike; enemy skirmish line, two deployed regiments compelled to withdraw by 'a half dozen well-directed shells and a telling carbine fire from behind a line of stone fence'. NOT supported: 15:00-17:00 hours, 10th NY skirmishers on Brinkerhoff Ridge, 2nd Va (Stonewall Bde) as the opponent, Rank's guns, 1st NJ short of carbine ammunition fighting with revolvers, 3rd PA north of the road (p956 shows 1st NJ mounted and 3rd PA dismounted skirmishers, undated on the page).

passage: until 6.30 p. m., when the First (Williams') Division and the First and Second Brigades of the Second Division were ordered from my right, leaving the intrenchments of Kane's brigade and Williams' division unoccupied on the withdrawal of the troops.
note: 18:30 departure, Greene left to hold the whole line, and the empty works supported (Greene p856; Geary p826-827: 'leaving one brigade to occupy the line of works of the entire corps'; Geary p826: 137th NY 'changed front, forming at a right angle to the rifle-pits, thus covering the right of the entire brigade'). Geary p833 lists the five NY regiments and a Third Brigade figure of 1,424 'taken into the engagement' (OCR table garbled; whole engagement, not a count at 18:30). NOT supported: 'about 800 yd (was about 300 yd in the morning)', works 'about 5 ft high' with head logs (secondary HN-KING). Do not use the modern rebuilt profile.

passage: until 7 p. m. of July 2, when, after changing position to the left of Jones' brigade, it Avas ordered forward in line of battle toward the heights in front, about three-quarters of a mile.
note: Nicholls' brigade (under Col. J. M. Williams) ordered forward at 7 p.m. Jul 2; Greene p856 attacked 'a few minutes before 7 p. m.'; Johnson p504: 'Jones' brigade in advance, followed by Nicholls' and Steuart's' and 'By the time my other brigades had crossed Rock Creek and reached the base of the mountain, it was dark'. Units, ~19:00 onset and Rock Creek crossing supported (onset vs 'dark' is an OR hour range). The sun altitude/azimuth/sunset/twilight text is computed (ephemeris), not an OR claim. Note: Johnson p501 (cited by shard) deals with an earlier action, not Jul 2.

passage: As soon as the attack commenced, i sent to General Wadsworth, commanding the division of the First Corps on our left, and to General Howard, commanding the Eleventh Corps, posted on the left of the First Corps, for assistance, to which they promptly responded
note: Greene asks Wadsworth (I Corps) and Howard (XI Corps) for help 'as soon as the attack commenced' (about 19:00, not 19:45); Schurz p731: four XI Corps regiments (157th NY, 61st Ohio, 82nd Ill, 45th NY); Greene p857: regiments 'relieved from thirty to ninety minutes by others with fresh ammunition and clean arms'. Geary p827 (R293) totals: 355 men from Wadsworth and about 400 from Howard (about 755). Greene names three XI Corps regiments, Schurz four. NOT supported: 19:45 hour, Wadsworth's three regiments by name beyond Greene's list.

passage: it again engaged him with an almost incessant fire for four hours, pending which several attempts to carry the works by assault, being entirely unsupported on the right (Jones' brigade having failed to hold its line on the right), were attended with more loss than success
note: Williams (Nicholls' brigade): ordered forward 7 p.m., almost incessant fire for four hours; Greene p856 four charges 7-9.30 p.m.; Geary p827 two and a half hours; Godard p861 (60th NY) close fire about two hours; Johnson p504: Jones wounded. Duration 'about 4 hours' for Nicholls supported; the row's ~20:30 start is not (OR 19:00). NOT supported: Jones vs 60th NY and Nicholls vs 78th/102nd NY pairings, Jones attacking 'the steepest slope', 'few Union losses', muzzle flash/moon haze (not OR).
Computed moonrise/altitude (ephemeris_1863.json), Jacobs cirrus and moonlight lux not OR claims. Not OR-checkable.

passage: The Thirty-seventh and Tenth Virginia and First Maryland Battalion then came to the assistance of the Twenty-third Virginia, and fully occupied the works.
note: Steuart's brigade (23rd, then 37th and 10th Va and 1st Md Bn) occupies the captured Union works and holds them (p510-511; 'During the night, the enemy advanced their line some distance beyond the breastworks, but were driven back to them again'); Colgrove p813: skirmishers 'returned with 23 prisoners' and learned 'Jones' and Steuart's brigades occupied our works', recovery 'deemed unsafe ... owing to the darkness of the night'; Morse p817 (2nd Mass): 'A company (F) of skirmishers was sent out, and they took 23 prisoners'; Ireland p866-867: 137th NY one man deep in Kane's works, enemy on right flank 'about 7.30 o'clock', fell back to the Third Brigade works. NOT supported on cited pages: ~21:00 hour, 'loses almost one third' (not an OR figure), 14th Brooklyn driving them back, 6th Wisconsin running into their fire, 71st PA sent by Hancock, '23rd and 10th Va outflank the 137th NY'.

passage: More, however, might have been done had not the impression at this time prevailed that we were firing upon our friends, and the fire been discontinued at intervals.
note: Steuart documents a mistaken-identity episode ('the impression ... prevailed that we were firing upon our friends'), but names no unit pair. The row's '1st NC fires on the 1st Md Battalion' is not in the OR (source W-CH, Wikipedia). The general episode may be shown without naming units; the unit pair stays a gap.

passage: The enemy, meeting with so determined a resistance, discontinued their attack at about lOp.
note: Geary: enemy discontinued the attack at about 10 p.m. (OCR 'lOp.'); Greene p856: four charges between 7 and 9.30 p.m.; Steuart p511: whole command rested from about 11 p.m. (OCR 'lip.') till about daylight. Johnson's attacks ending about 22:00 supported (range 21:30-23:00). NOT supported: whole-field fighting continuing to 22:30 (W-D2 secondary).

passage: The First and Third Brigades, of the Second Division, Cavalry Corps, arrived on the battle-field at Gettysburg, July 2, about noon
note: Gregg p956 describes the Jul 2 position at the right and a skirmish; it has no 'final night attack' on his position and no ~22:00 withdrawal to the Baltimore Pike. Only source is ST-GREGG (secondary). Visible gap.

passage: the medical officers had a sufficient supply of dressings, chloroform, and such articles until the supplies came up
note: Letterman p196-197 gives only general statements (chloroform and dressings carried with ambulances; surgeons worked day and night). No Spangler farm XI Corps hospital, four operating tables, forebay, lanterns, Brinton/Potter, nurses Hovey and Price, or patient counts. Sources secondary.

passage: To show the result of the system adopted upon my recommendation regarding transportation, and the effect of the system of field hospitals, I may here instance the hospital of the Twelfth Corps
note: Letterman p196 names no hospital sites for the III or V Corps (only the XII Corps hospital as an example). No White Run, Fiscel, Clapsaddle, Two Taverns, 300 yards from Rock Creek, or overnight moves. Row rests on HMDB markers (secondary).

passage: A few moments after General Weed, the brigade commander, had placed his command in position on this ridge, he was mortally wounded on the summit, near the battery.
note: Garrard p652 supports Weed mortally wounded on Little Round Top on Jul 2; Hazlett fell mortally wounded beside him. NOT supported: Weikert farm V Corps hospital, carried to the basement, dying before dawn, hour/date of death, amputated limbs piled outside a window. Do not transfer Hazlett's death 'at 8 p. m.' (Martin p660) to Weed.

passage: during a portion of the sitting of the council, which continued up to nearly 12 o'clock, fighting was going on on the right of our line
note: Gibbon (letter inside Meade's report) p127: council sat 'up to nearly 12 o'clock' (an end hour); minutes p73 'Minutes of council, July 2, 1863', replies from Gibbon ('would not retreat'), Williams ('Stay'), Birney, Sykes, Newton, Howard, Hancock, Sedgwick, Slocum (Birney also attends, the row omits him). Advising to hold supported. NOT supported: start hour, Leister house east room, Meade telling Gibbon the attack will come on his front. Same event as T2-216/T2-234.

Computed moon positions (ephemeris_1863.json), fog/dew an inference; no OR claim. Not OR-checkable. Shard recomputation: the printed illumination range '95%-86%' is contradicted by the computation (about 95-92%).
No OR citation; open gap (Lee's council of war, Lee-Longstreet conversation hour). OR vol.27 has no Lee council of war and no hour for such a conversation (per audit).

passage: After dark, I -withdre-w, and leaving a picket on the Hanover road, joined the rest of the division in rear of the enemy's breastworks
note: Broad outline supported: Walker p519 (withdrew after dark, picket on Hanover road, joined division behind the captured breastworks; 'At daylight next morning [3d], Steuart's brigade ... became hotly engaged'); Steuart p511 (whole command rested from about 11 p.m. till about daylight in the captured works; nearly 'during the night, the enemy advanced their line ... were driven back'); Rodes p556 (Daniel and O'Neal sent to Johnson, 'in position before daylight'); Williams p513 (Nicholls' brigade held a line about 100 yards from the Union works through the night). NOT in the OR: campfire policy, brigade-by-brigade overnight positions map, orders for the dawn attack, Smith's brigade here. Gap stays open with a narrower scope.

passage: At 1 a. m. of the 3d, Muhlenberg's (F, Fourth United States, six 12-poun(iers) and Kinzie's (K, Fifth United States, four 12-pounders) batteries were posted opposite the center of the line of the Twelfth Corps, so as to command the ravine formed by Rock Creek.
note: Hunt p237: 01:00 Jul 3, opposite the XII Corps center, commanding the Rock Creek ravine; 'The night of the 2d was devoted in great part to repairing damages, replenishing the ammunition chests, and reducing and reorganizing such batteries as had lost so many men and horses as to be unable efficiently to work the full number of guns.' Duplicate of T2-237.

passage: Night coming on, I held the ground until morning, when I found that the enemy had retreated from Hunterstown, leaving some of his wounded officers and men in the village.
note: Hampton: held the ground (met the enemy between Hunterstown and Gettysburg) until morning, then Jul 3 ordered through Hunterstown; Green p497: 'Fell back a mile, and took up another position, in which we remained until morning'. Hampton's brigade stayed in the Hunterstown-Gettysburg area overnight: supported. NOT supported: 'camps north of Gettysburg' (location not stated); the Union cavalry also stays/leaves differently (Hampton says the enemy retreated from Hunterstown).

passage: Soon after daylight, Rigby's battery (A, Maryland, six 3-inch) was also T)laced on the hill,
note: Muhlenberg and Kinzie at 01:00 (Hunt p237; Muhlenberg p870 'parallel to and on the southwest side of the Baltimore pike, almost directly opposite the center of the line formed by the Twelfth') supported. Rigby: Hunt 'Soon after daylight'; Tyler p873 'At daylight on July 3, Captain Rigby's battery ... opened fire, by direction of Major-General Slocum'; Rigby p899: 'On the morning of July 2, I was ordered to place my battery in position on a hill about 1 mile south of Gettysburg and 500 yards west of the Baltimore turnpike ... opened fire at about 2 o'clock' and 'At daylight on the morning of the 3d, I commenced shelling the woods'. 'Powers Hill' and 'McAllister Hill' are not OR names; NPS-H1 overnight Rigby placement is not in the OR. Conflict about when Rigby was on the hill (Jul 2 morning vs soon after daylight Jul 3).

passage: the breastworks on the left of swale, being the whole original position of the First and of part of the Third Brigade, were found to be occupied by the enemy in force.
note: Ruger p780 supports a XII Corps return to the works and discovery of the enemy in them (skirmishers/prisoners: Colgrove p813 'returned with 23 prisoners'), but places it on the night of Jul 2, not 02:00-04:00 Jul 3; Lockwood's brigade (p804) and Wallace (p808, 'reached the field of battle a short time before 8 o'clock') were not on Culp's Hill overnight. NOT supported: 'withdraw in the dark from the south slope' on Jul 3, 02:00-04:00 window, 'Spangler's Spring' scouts, a planned daybreak attack on these pages (Geary p827-828, not on the cited pages).

passage: our artillery, which had been posted to attack the enemy in the intrenchments of Kane's brigade and Williams' division, opened, and tlie attack was general on our line, and continued until 10.30 a.
note: Confederates held part of the lower-hill works at dawn (Ruger p780; Greene p857 'The enemy were early in the day driven from our intrenchments on our right'), Union artillery fired on them (Greene p857, Hunt p237), Greene's brigade held the upper line; Godard p860: 60th NY 'threw up intrenchments, by order of General Greene'. NOT supported: the regiment-by-regiment hill layout (102nd/149th in the saddle, 137th on the lower crest, 78th in reserve), Wadsworth's line begun evening Jul 1, 6th Wisconsin with a dozen spades, 123rd NY works '10 rods in front of a stone wall', head-log dimensions. 'Damaged' state is inference.

passage: These officers were engaged assiduously, day and night, with little rest, until the 6th
note: Letterman p197 only says surgeons worked day and night; no Weikert hospital, no move east toward the Baltimore Pike, no 950 treated, no lantern-lit sites. Row rests on HN-WEIKERT (secondary). Visible gap.

passage: When ordered thus to leave my intrenchments, I received no specific instructions as to the object of the move, the direction to be taken, or the point to be reached, beyond the order to move by the right flank and to follow the First Division.
note: Geary p826: moved the First and Second Brigades right across Rock Creek 'to the turnpike across Rock Creek Bridge' with no specific instructions, later returned (Candy p836 'Remained in position until 3.45 a. m.'). OR hours are Jul 2 evening (departure about 19:00) with Kane returning about 21:00-22:00 and Candy about midnight; the row's overnight Jul 3 timing is not supported. Geary says 'no specific instructions', not that he 'misread orders'; march 'down the Baltimore Pike' is not stated by name.

passage: During the night the line was strengthened as much as possible with rails, stones, and earth thrown up with sticks and boards, no tools being obtainable.
note: Same as T2-241. Hall p437, Curtis p450 ('the rails were nearly covered with earth by daylight'), Harrow p420, Tyler p873 ('all the reserve batteries (twelve in number) ... in position'; 'The infantry had constructed a slight breastwork') support strengthening overnight and reserve batteries in position. The row's note that rail/earth reinforcement is 'unverified (gap)' is contradicted for Hall's sector. NOT supported: that it was applied to 'the stone wall' or that the Angle wall is a pre-existing farm wall (NPS-ANGLE, secondary), Hunt personally bringing batteries (Hunt p237 only gives 'replaced by others from the Artillery Reserve').

passage: The regiments in the intrenchments were relieved from thirty to ninety minutes by others Avith fresh ammunition and clean arms,
note: Greene p857: regiments in the intrenchments relieved every thirty to ninety minutes by others with fresh ammunition and clean arms (rotation to clean arms/reload supported for the fighting period); Ireland p867: 'the enemy advanced with a yell and opened on us' (about 4 a.m.). NOT supported: the specific 'before dawn' hour and 'sends regiments to the rear to rest' wording (Greene describes a rotation inside the line during the fight).

passage: At night this ridge, naturally strong, was strengthened by building a stone wall about half way down the slope, wherever the rocks offered no protection to theinen.
note: Garrard (commanding Weed's brigade) p652: stone wall built at night about half way down the Round Top ridge slope; Fisher p658: Reserves ascend at 10 p.m. and throw up a stone wall across the ravine between the two hills. Night of Jul 2 construction by Weed's brigade (91st PA, 140th and 146th NY, 155th PA) and by Fisher's Reserves supported; no hour; 'south slope', Ohio battery, 'five Pennsylvania Reserve regiments' as Weed's brigade, and the NPS/Wikipedia attribution are not in these passages. Do not use the rebuilt modern wall for profile.

passage: I received orders from Colonel Alexander, commanding reserve artillery, to take position on the field before dayliglit,
note: Eshleman p434: placed before daylight; 'the left of my line had better be thrown a little to the rear' to avoid enfilade when day broke; 'Major Dearing afterward took position with his battalion on my left, and five guns of Colonel Cabell's battalion were placed in position between Captains Norcom and Richardson'; guns 'opened upon them moderately'; 'I was deprived of the services of Capt. Joe Norcom early in the day, who, being struck by a piece of shell, had to retire'.

passage: First South Carolina Volunteers [Provisional Army], in charge of a select battalion of sharpshooters, received a wound from which he died in a few minutes on the field.
note: Duplicate of T2-248. Engelhard p658 only mentions Capt. Haskell of the 1st SC (Provisional Army) commanding a select battalion of sharpshooters, mortally wounded; no rounds-per-man figure, no 'over 200 rounds by morning of Jul 3'. Source is American Rifleman (secondary). Visible gap.

passage: Sleeping on the field that night, and replacing ammunition, at dawn I again placed the whole battalion in position for the attack upon the enemy's new line.
note: Alexander p430: replaced ammunition that night; at dawn placed the whole battalion for the attack on the enemy's new line; losses 'killed, 19; wounded, 114; missing, 6; total, 139 men ... Horses killed and disabled in action, 116' (plus 2 killed, 3 wounded Mississippians at Moody's guns, outside the 139). NOT verified on cited page: battery roster 'Huger's batteries (Moody, Parker, Taylor, Rhett under Gilbert)' as written, 'spends most of the morning deploying artillery'.

passage: the breastworks on the left of swale, being the whole original position of the First and of part of the Third Brigade, were found to be occupied by the enemy in force.
note: Same as T2-244: Ruger p780 and Colgrove p813 ('They shortly returned with 23 prisoners, and reported that the enemy held our works on the left in large force'; 'It was also ascertained from the prisoners that Jones' and Steuart's brigades occupied our works') place the discovery in the darkness of the night of Jul 2, not about 04:00 Jul 3. At 03:45-04:30 Jul 3 the OR has Union batteries opening (Candy 3.45, Greene 4, Hunt 4.30). Event supported, ~04:00 hour contradicted; 'Spangler's Spring' not named.

passage: Captain McCarthy, who had, early in the morning, been placed 300 or 400 yards in advance of the skirmishers, fired 20 rounds, and, witli a section of another battery, succeeded in driving back an advancing line of the enemy.
note: Cabell p375: McCarthy placed early in the morning 300-400 yards in advance of the skirmishers, fired 20 rounds, and with a section of another battery drove back an advancing line of the enemy. The 'small brick house' in the same report belongs to other guns of the battalion ('placed several hundred yards in front of the infantry, near a small brick house'), and the report says McCarthy's position was 'considerably to the left of the brick house'. Row merges the two; the hour is 'early in the morning'.
Computed astronomy (ephemeris_1863.json) and Jacobs weather transcribed by secondary summaries; no OR claim. Not OR-checkable. Weather part not earned as documented.

passage: At 4.30 a. m. these batteries opened, and fired without intermission for fifteen minutes into the wood, at a range of from 600 to 800 yards.
note: Hunt p237: 04:30, fifteen minutes, 600-800 yards, Muhlenberg's and Kinzie's batteries; Muhlenberg p870 gives ten rifle + ten 12-pounder guns firing fifteen minutes at 600-800 yards. See T2-242 for the conflicting OR hours of the dawn fight (03:30-05:30).

passage: our artillery, which had been posted to attack the enemy in the intrenchments of Kane's brigade and Williams' division, opened, and tlie attack was general on our line, and continued until 10.30 a.
note: Union artillery opening on the Confederates in the works at dawn is supported, but the OR hours conflict: Geary p828 3.30 a.m. (artillery fire ten minutes); Kane p847 3.30 a.m. Confederate attack; Candy p836 3.45 a.m. battery; Greene p857 artillery opened and 'the attack was general' (about 4); Ireland p867 'enemy advanced with a yell' until relieved 5.45; Hunt p237 04:30 (15 minutes) and 05:30. NOT supported: 'five batteries (24 guns)', 'about 30 minutes of fire', 'planned attack by two of Geary's brigades' as a sequel (Geary p828 describes a simultaneous artillery and infantry attack at early dawn), 'wooded terrain keeps Confederate guns from replying'.

passage: Soon after daylight, Rigby's battery (A, Maryland, six 3-inch) was also T)laced on the hill
note: Hunt p237: Rigby's battery 'also placed on the hill' soon after daylight Jul 3; Tyler p873: 'At daylight on July 3, Captain Rigby's battery (A, First Maryland Artillery) opened fire, by direction of Major-General Slocum, upon the troops across Rock Creek'; Rigby p899: 'At daylight on the morning of the 3d, I commenced shelling the woods in my front, and continued firing slowly for about three hours.' All agree Rigby fired on the Culp's Hill woods from about daylight Jul 3. (Rigby says he had been on the hill since the morning of Jul 2: arrival conflict, see T3-022.)

passage: (early dawn) a simultaneous attack was made by artillery and the infantry of the Second dnd Third Brigades.
note: A dawn fight on the lower Culp's Hill works is documented, but the OR hours are all earlier than the row's ~05:00-05:30: Geary p828 3.30 a.m. 'early dawn'; Kane p847 attack 'commenced at 3.30 a.m.' by Johnson's division; Candy p836 3.45; Greene p857 4 a.m. (artillery opened, attack general); Ireland p867 enemy advanced with a yell, relieved 5.45; Steuart p511 'about daylight'; Williams 'early light'. Hunt's 04:30 and 05:30 are artillery times. Row's hour is outside every OR value; no default.

passage: The next day, July 3, it moved to Westminster, to guard the trains of the army at that point.
note: Buford p928: division moved to Westminster on Jul 3 to guard the trains; Gregg p956: 'the Second Brigade having been sent to Westminster' (Huey's brigade, not engaged on the field). OR separates places by unit and day (Buford's division Taneytown Jul 2 then Westminster Jul 3; Reserve Brigade Emmitsburg Jul 2 then the field Jul 3), so the row's source conflict is real. Merritt's Reserve Brigade text on p943 was not located in the cited page. NOT supported: 'Rummel farm region / Union cavalry assembly'; Buford's Emmitsburg destination.

passage: General Longstreet's dispositions were not completed as early as was ex]jected, but before notice could be sent to General Ewell. General Johnson had already become engaged, and it was too late to recall him.
note: Lee p320 and Ewell p447 ('Half an hour after Johnson attacked, and when too late to recall him, I received notice that Longstreet would not attack until 10 o'clock') support 'too late to recall' Johnson. NOT supported: the dialogue (Lee asks Ewell to delay; Ewell answers it is too late) - in the OR the notice never reached Ewell before Johnson was engaged; no hour except 'half an hour after Johnson attacked'.

passage: and at 5.30 a. m. all the tiatteries opened, and continued firing at intervals until 10 a. m., wlien the infantry succeeded in driving out the enemy
note: Hunt p237: at 5.30 a.m. all the batteries opened and fired at intervals until 10 a.m., when the infantry drove the enemy out (and reoccupied their position of the day before); Muhlenberg p870 agrees. NOT supported: 'Powers Hill guns' by name (OR uses 'the hill', 'Slocum's headquarters'); that attribution rests on HN-THUNDER (secondary).

passage: On the morning of July 3, pursuant to instructions from the commanding general (the ground along our line of battle being totally impracticable for cavalry operation's), I moved forward to a position t-o the left of General Ewell's left, and in advance of it,
note: Stuart: Jul 3 morning, 'pursuant to instructions from the commanding general', moved to a position left of Ewell's left on the Confederate left. No hour given (matches the row's 'hour not given'). The instruction itself is described by Stuart, not quoted from Lee.

passage: The command expended in the fight on July 3, and in subsequent skirmishing, 277,000 rounds of ammunition.
note: Geary p833 footnote gives 277,000 rounds 'in the fight on July 3, and in subsequent skirmishing' (not 227,000 or about 250,000 as the row; single-witness OCR digits, period differs from the row's). Walker p519 (after five hours' incessant firing a Rodes brigade came up; renewed attack failed), Johnson p504 (Stonewall Brigade ordered up, assault renewed, Daniel's and Rodes' (O'Neal) brigades reported, 'two other assaults were made') support failed Confederate assaults. NOT supported: Smith's brigade on these pages, the 06:00-11:00 window as stated, the 227,000/250,000 figures, 'close log fence works damaged by shell fire'.

passage: Pickett, with three of his brigades, joined Longstreet the following morning
note: No OR passage says an order did or did not reach Pickett to be on the field by daylight or that preparation took all morning (W-PC, secondary). Related OR facts: Lee (Jul 1863 report) p308 Pickett joined Longstreet the morning of Jul 3; Lee Jan 1864 p320 says afternoon of Jul 2 (conflict); Peyton p385 (Garnett's brigade): 'they reached the field about 9 a. m.' on Jul 3. Gap stays open.
